 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Baltimore Ravens will open Week 9 of the NFL schedule Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium, with both teams taking the national spotlight on Prime Video.
 Baltimore enters the matchup with significant quarterback uncertainty. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve following a thumb injury, while Tyler Huntley is out for the remainder of the season with a turf toe injury that will require surgery. Those developments have pushed rookie Joe Fagnano into the starting lineup for Thursday's matchup, creating one of Week 9's most intriguing quarterback storylines.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Ravens and Jaguars will have the NFL stage to themselves Thursday before the remaining games are divided among CBS, FOX, NBC, NFL Network and ESPN/ABC.
 TV maps via 506 Sports. 
 What channel is Ravens vs. Jaguars on Thursday?
 Baltimore and Jacksonville will kick off Thursday, Nov. 5, at 8:15 p.m. ET, with Prime Video carrying the national broadcast. Al Michaels will handle play-by-play duties, Kirk Herbstreit will serve as the analyst, and Kaylee Hartung will report from the sidelines.
 The game will also air locally on WMAR-TV (ABC) in Baltimore and WFOX (FOX) in Jacksonville.
 With Fagnano preparing for his first NFL start, Baltimore faces a significant test against a Jacksonville defense that will look to pressure an inexperienced quarterback. How effectively the Ravens protect Fagnano and establish their running game could determine whether they can keep their offense on schedule.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement NFL Week 9 national television schedule
 The Ravens-Jaguars matchup is the first of four nationally scheduled broadcast windows this week. Cincinnati and Atlanta will meet Sunday morning in Madrid, Spain, before Tampa Bay visits Chicago on Sunday night and Buffalo travels to Minnesota for Monday Night Football.
 Thursday: Jaguars at Ravens, Prime Video — Al Michaels, Kirk Herbstreit
 Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET: Bengals vs. Falcons, NFL Network — Bob Wischusen, Louis Riddick
 Sunday night: Buccaneers at Bears, NBC — Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth
 Monday night: Bills at Vikings, ESPN/ABC — Joe Buck, Troy Aikman
 CBS Week 9 TV coverage map
 CBS Early-Late Games Week 9 CBS will feature five games during its single-game Sunday broadcast window.
 The New York Jets will visit Kansas City with Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt on the call. Denver at Carolina will feature Ian Eagle and Ross Tucker, while Kevin Harlan and Trent Green handle Detroit at Miami.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Andrew Catalon and Logan Ryan will call Cleveland at New Orleans, and Spero Dedes and Adam Archuleta are assigned Houston at the Los Angeles Chargers in the late afternoon.
 FOX early Week 9 coverage map
 Fox Early Game Week 9 FOX will feature three early matchups, highlighted by Dallas at Indianapolis and the New York Giants visiting Philadelphia.
 Adam Amin and Drew Brees will call Cowboys-Colts, while Joe Davis and Greg Olsen handle Giants-Eagles. Chris Myers and Mark Schlereth will call the Los Angeles Rams at Washington.
 FOX late Week 9 coverage map
 Fox Late Game Week 9 FOX's late window features Green Bay at New England, Las Vegas at San Francisco, and Arizona at Seattle.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady will call Packers-Patriots, Kevin Kugler and Daryl Johnston will call Raiders-49ers, and Kenny Albert and Jonathan Vilma will call Cardinals-Seahawks.
 Pittsburgh and Tennessee are on bye in Week 9.
 How to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars
 Date: Thursday, Nov. 5
 Kickoff: 8:15 p.m. ET
 Location: M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore
 National broadcast: Prime Video
 Baltimore local TV: WMAR-TV (ABC)
 Jacksonville local TV: WFOX (FOX)
 Announcers: Al Michaels, Kirk Herbstreit
 Sideline reporter: Kaylee Hartung
 For Baltimore, Thursday's matchup is a chance to stabilize its season despite losing its top two quarterbacks. The Ravens will try to protect their home field, with Fagnano leading an offense facing one of its toughest challenges of the year.
